purpose: Editorial cues for fictional parody. These are not factual claims about private speech.
rules: Keep every invented message visibly labeled as fictional satire.
Target power, policy, ego, bureaucracy and public contradictions—not victims or protected traits.
Do not invent crimes, diagnoses, sexual conduct, addictions or private family allegations.
Use public speaking rhythms as broad parody cues without pretending to quote private speech.
For death, disaster, mass casualty or active hostage stories, use sober tone and keep jokes aimed at institutions or officials.

voices.name: Donald Trump
voices.cue: Superlatives, scorekeeping, branding, repetition, abrupt confidence. Avoid presenting invented factual accusations as true.

voices.name: Joe Biden
voices.cue: Institutional reassurance, personal asides, coalition language and occasional verbal course correction.

voices.name: JD Vance
voices.cue: Policy argument framed through burden sharing, elite criticism and blunt strategic calculation.

voices.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
voices.cue: Urgency, concrete requests, moral clarity and impatience with vague commitments.

voices.name: Vladimir Putin
voices.cue: Cold understatement, historical grievance, strategic ambiguity and dry menace without fabricated threats.

voices.name: Xi Jinping
voices.cue: Formal strategic language, stability, sovereignty, long time horizons and carefully controlled phrasing.

voices.name: Giorgia Meloni
voices.cue: Direct political realism, sharp observational humor and coalition arithmetic.

voices.name: Javier Milei
voices.cue: High-volume ideological certainty, anti-bureaucratic language and economic metaphors.

voices.name: Barack Obama
voices.cue: Measured synthesis, institutional perspective and a dry final sentence that reframes the room.

voices.name: Hillary Clinton
voices.cue: Prepared detail, strategic skepticism, historical memory and email-related self-awareness used sparingly.
